Hi Sarah / Michael \u0014

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we can align on a PoC scope:

What we heard
- Primary goal: enable FinApps to surface ERP/invoicing actions via LLM-driven assistant inside the customer portal.
- Priorities: secure auth (SSO + KMS for keys), predictable latency for interactive UI flows, and safe tool invocation with robust error handling.
- Data & infra constraints: customer data must remain in your VPC for the PoC; key management via your KMS is preferred.

Key integration areas to validate
1) SDK setup & auth
   - Lightweight JS/TS SDK for frontend + server-side SDK for backend calls
   - Auth options: short-lived API tokens from your KMS-backed broker OR OAuth with customer identity (we recommended token broker for initial PoC)
2) Routing & fallbacks
   - Region routing + model variant fallback to keep UI responsive if dedicated capacity saturates
3) Tool/function calling (structured output)
   - Define tool schemas (name, inputs, outputs, idempotency tokens) and map to backend endpoints (ERP, payments, search)
   - Support for parallel tool invocation where helpful (e.g., call both ledger-check and pricing-service concurrently and consolidate results)
4) Embeddings & rerankers
   - Hybrid approach: local embeddings for company docs + Redwood-hosted reranker for recall precision

Attachments: integration checklist + architecture diagram (both attached).

Proposed next steps
- Tech deep-dive with FinApps infra team (30\u201345m) \u0014 include your infra/identity people and our Dev.
- Share minimal sample payloads and expected error cases before the call.
- We\u0019ll provide a short PoC plan (2\u20133 week scope) and sample SDK snippet for auth/token exchange.

Can you confirm preferred auth approach (token broker vs OAuth) and availability for a tech call next week?

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Li <sli@finapps.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-04-07T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinApps - Tool-calling integration post-call recap & next steps

Hi Sarah / Michael \u0014

Happy to dig into the technical approach. Below are concise recommendations and patterns we use at Redwood for tool/function calling, auth, routing, and embeddings/rerankers. I\u0019ll be prepared to walk through any of these on the tech call.

1) Tool registry & definitions- We recommend keeping canonical tool definitions versioned in your repo (JSON/YAML). Each tool definition includes: name, description, input schema (JSON-schema v4), output schema, idempotency semantics, allowed callers, and rate limits.
- Example (conceptual):
  {
    "name": "create_invoice",
    "inputs": {"customer_id": "string", "line_items": "array"},
    "outputs": {"invoice_id": "string", "status": "string"},
    "idempotency_key": "optional",
    "timeout_ms": 3000
  }

- Redwood can host a lightweight registry for PoC, but long-term we recommend you own the source-of-truth and push the schema to Redwood via an API or CI pipeline so our runtime enforces validation.

2) Tool choice & orchestration patterns- Sync vs Async: For blocking UI flows (create invoice), execute synchronously with a tight timeout and optimistic UI; for longer-running tasks kick an async workflow and return a correlation id.
- Parallel tools: our runtime supports parallel invocations through a fan-out primitive. Results are returned as a list; orchestration code (either on your side or via Redwood actions) merges/chooses the final output.
- Conflict resolution: include scoring metadata and deterministic tie-breakers in the tool output so the aggregator can select the highest-confidence result.

3) Error handling & retries- Best practices:
  - Retries: idempotent tools get exponential backoff (max 3 attempts). Non-idempotent tools should not be retried automatically.
  - Partial failure: if one of N parallel tools fails, return partial results with an explicit errors array and let the assistant surface graceful fallback options to the user.
  - Circuit breaker: track error rate and fail fast to a safe fallback model variant or canned response.
  - Observability: attach request_id and tool_call_id to every call for tracing.

4) Auth & token flow- PoC: token-broker pattern (short-lived tokens minted by your auth proxy, backed by your KMS).
- Prod: mutual TLS between Redwood runtime and your tool endpoints or signed JWTs with KMS-managed keys.
- Secrets: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for encrypting persistent credentials and will not store plaintext keys.

5) Routing & fallbacks- You can specify routing policies by region, latency SLO, or cost tier. Specify primary -> secondary model variants and a fallback action (e.g., call cached response or lighter-weight model) when thresholds are breached.

6) Structured output & safety- Use strict JSON schemas for any tool-calling responses. Redwood's runtime can validate the assistant's proposed tool invocation against the schema and reject unsafe or malformed calls.

7) Embeddings & rerankers- Common pattern: generate dense embeddings for your docs (stored in your vector DB) and run a lightweight candidate retrieval locally, then call Redwood's hosted reranker as a secondary step for precision. For PII-sensitive corpora, you can host both retrieval and reranker inside your VPC with Redwood calling into it via secure endpoints.

PoC commitments: We can support a 2-week sprint for an initial PoC once scope is locked. Typical PoC tasks:
- Week 1: token-broker auth + SDK setup + one sample tool implemented (create_invoice)
- Week 2: parallel tool fan-out + structured output validation + basic embeddings/re-rank demo

I\u0019ll include short example SDK snippets and a checklist on the call.
